title: Preemption attenuation sketch and regional handshake log - 2026-04-29
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick working notes from the week: exploratory sketch for reducing the customer-visible impact of preemption events across regions. Goal: reduce tail latency and error spikes during spot eviction or host reclamation without blowing up cost or complexity.

High-level idea (sketch): preemption attenuation = layered soft-failures + proactive handshake
- Instead of immediate hard kill or immediate full-migrate fallback, introduce a short attenuation window (30–90s) where we: 
  - start a lightweight replication of the hottest model shards to an adjacent region (read-only priming)
  - pause non-critical background work (model downloads, heavy diagnostics) on the affected node to free network/IO
  - enable an in-flight request buffer that prefers retry to immediate fallback (if latency budget allows)
- Handshake mechanism: region A emits a PREEMPTION_SOON signal with metadata (affected slot id, model fingerprint, expected TTL). Neighboring region B responds with ACCEPT_PRIMING or DECLINE depending on spare slot budget and latency class. If ACCEPT_PRIMING, pre-copy of small KV cache and model prefix occurs.

Why this might help (notes to self):
- Many customer errors during preemption are caused by abrupt eviction of a slot that still has hot KV cache; warming an adjacent slot reduces cold-start latency and avoids repeated fallbacks to higher-cost models.
- Handshake keeps us from overloading other regions: we only priming when neighbors can accept.
- Keeps SLO-friendly behavior for low-latency tiers while sacrificing longer-running batch jobs first.

Key constraints and risk areas:
- Network cost of priming (especially cross-region) could be non-trivial. Need to estimate bytes for typical KV/cache snapshot and model prefix sizes. Action: Diego to run a bytes-per-eviction sample. (JIRA:INF-4176)
- Race conditions: if eviction happens faster than the handshake completes we still need a safe fallback. Proposed fallback: immediate failover to smaller model variant + ticketing for customer-facing retries.
- Security: priming copies must honor tenant isolation and KMS/ACLs. Coordinate with security for KMS flows.

Experiment plan (mini-sprint):
1) Simulation harness (2 days): build a fake preemption emitter that can tell a neighbor to accept/decline. Measure handshake latency and priming throughput. Owner: Marcus.
2) Byte budget measurement (3 days): sample real KV cache sizes across representative workloads (chat, instruction, embeddings). Owner: Diego.
3) Canary integration (1 week): on a low-traffic region (eu-west-2), wire attenuation as opt-in mode for non-enterprise customers. Collect error spikes, tail-latency, and cost delta. Owner: Aisha.
4) Roll decision (post-metrics): if tail 99.9% latency improves by >20% with <8% cross-region bandwidth cost, consider scaling to other regions.

Standup log snippets (week):
- Mon 2026-04-27: brainstormed handshake messages and minimal metadata. Attendees: Aisha, Marcus. Outcome: simple schema with slot_id, model_sha, ttl, priority_class.
- Tue 2026-04-28: ran priming throughput test in staging. Observed 120MB/s effective cross-region copy when chunked; aggressive chunk sizes caused jitter on concurrent requests. Note: reduce chunk size to 4MB to smooth bursts.
- Wed 2026-04-29: met with SRE on backpressure semantics. Decided: when priming triggers, apply token-bucket backpressure to background IO to preserve request latencies.
- Thu 2026-04-30: security review request opened for KMS implications. Action: add confluence page with KMS flow diagrams.

Metrics to capture in the canary: (minimum)
- preemption-triggered 5xx rate (per-customer)
- tail latency (p95/p99/p99.9) for affected routes
- cross-region bytes used for priming per-eviction
- successful handshake rate (accepted/declined)
- cost delta estimate (bandwidth + small extra slot hours)

Runbook excerpt (first-draft):
- Detection: preemption-warning from cloud provider => mark slot as PREEMPTION_SOON and annotate TTL.
- Handshake: attempt handshake to up to 2 preferred neighbors (region preference list). If both decline, fall back to local fast-fail policy.
- Priming: stream KV/cache snapshot in 4MB chunks with token-bucket limit of X MB/s (X derived from region spare capacity).
- Failback: if priming not complete at eviction, increase routing weight to primed neighbor if present; otherwise route to smaller model variant.
- Postmortem tags: attach INF-ATTENUATION tag and export trace id for correlation.

Open questions and TODOs:
- How do we pick neighbors? Topology + latency matrix needed. Action: Marcus to pull the intra-region latency matrix.
- TTL semantics: what is the minimum TTL the cloud provider gives on preemption messages? We need benchmarks. Action: SRE to simulate real preemption timing distribution.
- Cost modeling: quick estimate needed before wide canary. Diego to produce a 2-week cost delta projection.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Marcus: simulation harness & latency matrix (ETA 2026-05-05)
- Diego: KV/cache size sampling + cost projection (ETA 2026-05-06)
- Aisha: canary plan and traffic routing rules for eu-west-2 (ETA 2026-05-08)
- Lena: open security review ticket and draft KMS flow in confluence (ETA 2026-05-04)

Notes-to-self / brainstorming scraps (informal):
- Could we do region-local priming only (no cross-region) and rely on multi-AZ warm slots? Might reduce bandwidth cost at the expense of reduced availability in small regions.
- Consider soft-priority: only priming for enterprise and high-latency-sensitive routes initially.
- Think about telemetry: add a small metric for "primed-by-eviction" on slot metrics so we can correlate priming with improved cold-starts.

Related links and references (internal):
- INF-4123: preemption-propagation-ticket (design notes)
- confluence://capacity/attenuation-proposal-2026 (sketch + diagrams)

Quick retrospective: the week felt productive; the handshake idea reduced our initial failure modes in the staging sim. Still lots of unknowns but we have concrete next steps. Keep this doc as the scratchpad for the next two sprints; will formalize into a runbook once the canary produces metric evidence.

-- Aisha
